holidays.name: National Iced Tea Day
holidays.description: A day to pour a tall, frosty glass of iced tea and toast the planet's favorite chilled brew, sweet or unsweet, with lemon or without.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States in the heart of summer, it celebrates iced tea's rise as a staple beverage. The drink gained widespread popularity at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair, where a heat wave pushed visitors to ask for tea over ice.
holidays.funFact: Americans drink billions of gallons of tea each year, and roughly 80 percent of it is consumed iced.

holidays.name: National Black Cow Day
holidays.description: A day for sipping a Black Cow, the classic soda fountain float made with root beer and vanilla ice cream, which is basically dessert you can drink through a straw.
holidays.origin: The Black Cow dates back to the late 1800s. Legend credits Frank J. Wisner of Cripple Creek, Colorado, who in 1893 supposedly noticed the moon rising over Cow Mountain and dropped vanilla ice cream into his root beer. Other soda fountains claim the invention too.
holidays.funFact: Depending on the region, a 'black cow' can mean root beer with vanilla ice cream, or cola with ice cream, and some places call the same drink a 'brown cow.'

holidays.name: National Herbs and Spices Day
holidays.description: A day to rescue those dusty jars in the back of your cabinet and give your cooking some flavor by trying a new herb or spice.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance created to encourage people to explore seasonings and flavors from around the world. Its exact founder is unclear, as with many food holidays.
holidays.funFact: Spices were once so valuable that pepper was used as currency in medieval Europe, and peppercorns were sometimes accepted to pay rent.

holidays.name: Ballpoint Pen Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the humble ballpoint pen, the trusty tool behind countless signatures, doodles, grocery lists, and stolen office supplies.
holidays.origin: It honors the patent of the ballpoint pen by Hungarian journalist László Bíró, who got the idea from watching newspaper ink dry quickly on the printing press. He patented his design in 1938 and refined it with his brother György.
holidays.funFact: Bíró's ballpoint pens were first adopted by the British Royal Air Force during World War II because they did not leak at high altitudes the way fountain pens did.

holidays.name: Time Management Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to getting your schedule under control, which for many people means making a to-do list and then procrastinating on it.
holidays.origin: This observance is a modern productivity-themed day promoted by workplace and self-improvement communities, encouraging people to prioritize tasks and make better use of their hours.
holidays.funFact: The Pomodoro Technique, a popular time management method, was named after a tomato-shaped kitchen timer used by its inventor, Francesco Cirillo, when he was a university student.
